correctness.rationale: Independent continuous uniform scores generate the specified independent voter permutations. Strong components of a tournament have uniformly oriented cross-edges and their condensation is a totally ordered tournament. Hence a fixed s-subset is the Smith set exactly if its own tournament is strongly connected and it beats every outsider. Conditional on its scores x, each outsider is forbidden by the union of the majority cylinder boxes with volume b(x), independently of other outsiders. The exact probability is therefore binom(n,s) times the integral of H(x)(1−b(x))^(n−s). At x=n^(−1/ℓ)y group the cylinders by their ℓ-coordinate voter subsets. The union within a group has volume n^−1 V_J(y) exactly; an intersection across distinct groups constrains at least ℓ+1 coordinates and contributes O(n^(−1−1/ℓ)) uniformly on bounded y. This yields the limiting kernel H(y) exp(−Φ(y)). For the global bound, b is at least the average of its s binom(m,ℓ) cylinder volumes, so the scaled kernels extended by zero are bounded by a product of e^(−a σ_ℓ(y_i)) with a>0 for n≥2s. To check integrability, order a row, let t be its ℓth-largest coordinate, and write the larger coordinates as t u_i with u_i≥1. The smaller coordinates contribute a factor proportional to t^(m−ℓ), and σ_ℓ is at least t^ℓ∏u_i. Integrating t then bounds the row integral by a finite constant times ∏∫₁^∞u^(−m/ℓ)du since m>ℓ. Dominated convergence gives L¹ convergence of scaled kernels. The binomial asymptotic and the score Jacobian give factor 1/s! and exponent ms/ℓ−s=s(ℓ−1)/ℓ. Positivity follows from three cyclic orders of three nonempty blocks (the directed inter-block cycle makes the whole tournament strongly connected), with the extra voters in opposite pairs; this gives an open positive-volume set of scores. Exchangeability for the increasing-label lists contributes the same binomial factor in the unnormalized conditional density, so normalizing cancels it and yields the stated TV convergence. The proof requires fixed ℓ,s, and the conditional law uses the specified score representation. The frozen finite-profile and rational overlap checks were inspected but not run; they do not prove either limit.

evidence: Berchenko–Liu use the same fixed odd voter count and uniform independent rankings; their fixed-s≥3 theorem gives a Θ(n^−s(ℓ−1)/ℓ) result with explicit bounds, not an equivalent. Their growing-size results do not give the fixed-size limit.
Sauermann’s sharp theorem has one candidate, with coefficient the integral of e^(−σ_ℓ); its kernel and mass convergence also give TV for s=1 by Scheffé’s lemma.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The one-candidate result is an exact boundary case, not a theorem on internally strongly connected cores of arbitrary fixed size. Bounds on the multi-candidate event do not identify an integral constant or a limiting density.

evidence: The former supplies the correct scaling with explicit upper and lower bounds; the latter supplies the exact scaled kernel for one candidate.

For multiple candidates it matters that same-voter-subset cylinder overlaps survive at order n^−1, whereas intersections across distinct voter subsets disappear at that order. H restricts the limiting law to the strongly connected ranking cones.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The one-candidate kernel cannot be multiplied across candidates: all face the same outside alternatives, and within-subset cylinder volumes are unions, not sums. The exact overlap term and L¹ control for this joint kernel go beyond the inspected order and singleton results; once that kernel convergence is proved, TV is a normalization consequence, not a separate priority claim.

residual_risks: An equivalent statement on top components under another name could have escaped the bounded searches. No exhaustive priority certification is inferred.

value.rationale: For a rare event in a standard voting model, the order theorem left the coefficient and the law of the conditioning event’s score geometry unresolved. The shared-outside-alternative union volumes distinguish the law from a product of one-candidate laws, and TV convergence controls bounded measurable features of this fixed-size core, not just its occurrence rate. This is a concrete probabilistic improvement within the fixed-parameter regime.
